# The wu025r005 wave mesh

*Generated by Claude.*

MESAWAVE runs WW3 on a global unstructured mesh: triangles whose corners (the nodes) are where WW3
keeps a full wave spectrum. A MOM6 grid stores neighbours implicitly as (i, j); an unstructured mesh
stores every node's position and every triangle's three corners. The project began with a NOAA
collaborator's mesh, `wu025r004`. Its in-house replacement is `wu025r005`, built with OceanMesh2D.
The code is in [`mesh/`](https://github.com/manishvenu/mesawave/tree/main/mesh) and its
[README](https://github.com/manishvenu/mesawave/blob/main/mesh/README.md) has the commands.

## What it is

The target spacing is set by a size raster made by `mesh/mesawave_mesh/regions.py`:

h = min(25, 10 + 0.15 d<sub>coast</sub>, 12 + 0.15 d<sub>TC</sub>, 5 + 0.15 max(d<sub>US</sub> − 100, 0)) km

where d is the distance in km to the coast, to the tropical-cyclone regions (convex hulls) and to the
US coast. So: 25 km in the open ocean, 10 km at coasts, 12 km in tropical-cyclone regions and 5 km
along the US coast, growing at 0.15 km per km between them.

| | `wu025r004` (NOAA) | `wu025r005` |
|---|---|---|
| Nodes | 1,671,039 | 1,285,928 (build `v2`, the one in use) |
| Spacing | 25 km open ocean, 10 km coasts, 5 km US coasts | as above, plus 12 km tropical-cyclone regions |

The proposal budgeted 1.2 million nodes; `v2` is about 7% over that and about 23% cheaper than
`wu025r004`. Its spacing is within 1% of the target (median) in every zone.

## How it is built

1. **Size raster** (`regions.py`): the formula above on a global grid, with distances from the GSHHS
   shoreline. It also writes the Antarctic ice-front coastline the mesh uses as its southern boundary.
2. **Size levels** (`size_levels`, [make_mesh.m:64](https://github.com/manishvenu/mesawave/blob/main/mesh/mesawave_mesh/make_mesh.m#L64)):
   the sizes that cover more than 1% of the raster, filled in geometrically so no step is more than 10%.
3. **Starting points** (`initial_points`, [make_mesh.m:76](https://github.com/manishvenu/mesawave/blob/main/mesh/mesawave_mesh/make_mesh.m#L76)):
   one regular triangle lattice per size level, in latitude rows. Each point is kept
   where its level is the nearest to the target size, and points on land are dropped. (Thinning one
   fine lattice at random instead left 26% of the nodes with a wrong number of neighbours, line 78.)
4. **Relaxation** (OceanMesh2D's DistMesh, line 42): edges act as springs that pull towards the target
   length; every 10 iterations points that are too close are removed and long edges are split. It
   stops at 100 iterations ("too many iterations, exit" in the log is normal).
5. **WW3 inputs** (`make_grid_inp.sh`): `ww3_grid` writes `mod_def.ww3`, and `ww3_msh_to_esmf.py`
   writes the ESMF mesh CESM's coupler uses, with one element per WW3 node.

`run_mesh.sh PREFIX SCALE` runs steps 2–4: SCALE 1 is the production mesh (about 50 min on 16 cores),
SCALE 4 a quick test with every size four times larger (about 80,000 nodes).

## The "dots": nodes with 5 or 7 neighbours

In a perfect equilateral lattice every node has 6 neighbours. A node with 5 or 7 is a defect, like a
dislocation in a crystal, and moving nodes around cannot remove it. A closed triangle mesh on a sphere
needs at least 12 five-neighbour nodes (an icosahedron has exactly that); the problem is having
thousands more.

`v2` started from latitude rows. Each row going poleward is shorter, and each change in row length
needs a 5/7 pair. `v2` staggers the rows so the pairs are scattered, but about 5,000 open-ocean nodes
(~1%) are still 5/7 pairs, and the triangles around them are about 1 km off the 25 km target.

## Option: icosahedral starting points

`v2`'s latitude rows stay the method in use. The icosahedral start is kept as an option
(`run_mesh.sh PREFIX SCALE SIZEFILE icos`): it removes the deep-ocean dots but adds a second lattice
function and a rotation script (`tools/icos_rotation.py`), and leaves streaks instead, so it is not worth
the extra code for now. Neither the dots nor the streaks have been tested for their effect on the waves.

Instead of rows, `initial_points_icos` ([make_mesh.m:106](https://github.com/manishvenu/mesawave/blob/main/mesh/mesawave_mesh/make_mesh.m#L106))
starts each level from a subdivided icosahedron (a "soccer ball"): 20 triangular faces, each filled
with a regular lattice, so every point has 6 neighbours except the 12 corners. The icosahedron is
rotated so 8 of its 12 corners fall on land. A step-by-step Python version is in
[`mesh/tools/icosphere_basics.ipynb`](https://github.com/manishvenu/mesawave/blob/main/mesh/tools/icosphere_basics.ipynb).

Open-ocean results (full size, 1.29 million nodes):

| Build | Iterations | 5/7 nodes | Deep 5/7 nodes (> 5 spacings from a coast or refined zone) | Edge length p5–p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v2` (rows) | 100 | 5,041 | 2,693 | 24.1–26.0 km |
| `icos_s1` | 100 | 1,464 | 2 | 23.3–26.8 km |
| `icos_s1_it700` | 700 | 1,053 | 62 | 23.3–26.7 km |

The icosahedral start removes almost all deep-ocean defects; the remaining ones sit where the size
changes, which needs them. The cost is a wider spread of edge lengths: placing the lattice on the sphere
stretches the faces, so edges along the icosahedron's seams come out near 23 km and face centres near
27 km. Median triangle quality is 0.994, against 0.9996 for `v2`. Quick SCALE 4 builds don't show the
stretch, so it has to be checked at full size.

**Why more iterations don't help.** Relaxation smooths like diffusion: a pattern N spacings wide needs
roughly N² iterations, and an icosahedron face is about 280 spacings across. Seven times more
iterations left the spread unchanged.

**An idea not tried: an equal-area start.** On one face (n = 30), the small triangles' areas run from 0.93 times
the mean at the face edges to 1.10 at the centre, a ratio of 1.19. An equal-area map from the flat face
to the sphere (Snyder's icosahedral projection, which the PROJ library provides) would make the areas
equal, but it distorts shapes, so the test is whether it narrows the edge-length spread, not just the
areas.
